analyst.summary: CreditAccess Grameen is India's largest and highest-quality rural microfinance lender, now recovering from a sector-wide credit stress cycle that hit microfinance lenders through FY25-FY26. Asset quality is genuinely improving (bad-loan ratio down sharply from a year ago, collections strong, credit costs normalizing), and management is also building a broader micro-retail lending business alongside its core microfinance book. The headline profit jump this quarter is largely a bounce-back from last year's stress-related provisions rather than new business growth, and the stock has already re-rated meaningfully to price in the recovery. We rate it a Hold: good business, but not cheap at current levels, and microfinance remains a cyclical, regulation-sensitive segment.
